name: Zero Waste

established.purpose: Enterprise fund for refuse, recycling and organics collection, the transfer station and street sweeping, funded by customer rates

legal_basis: Enterprise fund; rates set by Council under Proposition 218 majority-protest procedures; current five-year schedule FY2024-2028 adopted June 27, 2023 (Resolution 70,932-N.S.)

annual.note: Proprietary funds statement, ACFR FY2024 p.87-88. Operating loss $5,416,107; change in net position -$3,974,790
Proprietary funds statement, ACFR FY2025 p.85-86. Operating loss $1,471,134; change in net position -$1,272,826; net position $349,593 after restatement at year start

flows.instrument: Council Item 49, Resolution 70,932-N.S., five-year rate schedule FY2024-2028 (Proposition 218 hearing)
flows.stated_reason: Raise refuse, recycling and organics rates; staff projected the fund stays positive but its balance falls from $24.5M to $3.3M over the five years, and goes negative before the end of FY2025 without the increase
flows.note: Amount: the schedule gives rates by cart size, not a total; the revenue effect is not stated as one figure. Residential 20-gallon cart $33.30/month in FY2024.

flows.to_fund: Capital Improvement Fund $735,058 (capital project support); Catastrophic Insurance $110,870
flows.stated_reason: Capital project support and catastrophic insurance

flows.instrument: Audit Status Reports, Council Items 31 and 32, March 10, 2020; Auditor's dashboard
flows.stated_reason: 18 of 27 recommendations from the 2014 and 2016 Zero Waste audits dropped, including a route audit to align billing with service, franchise-fee recovery on recyclables, and biweekly garbage collection (about $496K/yr, needing a state waiver)
flows.note: Amount: the one dropped item with a figure is $496,000 a year; the others were not sized.

obligations.note: Transfer Station replacement (pre-construction funded by the 2023 rates) and electric fleet conversion (about $9.0M vehicles plus $6.5M chargers, per the fleet audit status report)

status.years_in_deficit: Operating losses in FY2024 and FY2025 despite the 2023 rate schedule; net position near zero
open_questions: Whether the 2023 rate schedule's balance projection ($3.3M by FY2028) still holds given losses of $4.0M and $1.3M in its first two years.
The timing and cost of the Transfer Station replacement.
Which of the 18 dropped audit recommendations the FY2027-28 budget revisits.
